nodes.partnerMessage:
Deadbolt's locked and the curtains are shut. Okay, you're officially in the vault, {PlayerName}.

Before I put the reels on, promise me one thing: you won't pass this stuff around. I've already had years of work taken from me once.

choices.choiceText: Strictly classified with me, Evelyn. You have my absolute word.
Leak it? I don't even know what I'm looking at yet. Show me the data.
Relax with the spy roleplay. It's just old tape reels, not state secrets.
Skip the text logs for now. Call my line and brief me directly.

nodes.partnerMessage:
...Thank you. Seriously. I didn't realize how tense I was until I read that.

I've spent days rescuing pieces of tape that should've been ruined years ago. Handing them to someone else is a lot more personal than it sounds.

choices.choiceText: Your research is sacred to you. I treat it with the same respect.
Take a breath, Evelyn. What's the master reel on this drive?
Baking magnetic acetate? Isn't that for sticky-shed syndrome?
Who stole your research before? What happened to them?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Alright, straight to it. I like that.

This was recorded at the mountain observatory at 3:14 in the morning. There's a really strange spike around 18 Hz. It's below what most people can hear, but you can see it clearly in the data:

choices.choiceText: That waveform isn't random background hum. The comb filtering is deliberate.
Looks like an electrical ground loop from an old transformer down the road.
Honestly, it looks like audio artifact scribble. Anyone could fake this in Audacity.
Why was the recording taken specifically at 3:14 AM?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Okay... that actually got under my skin. I know it's just old tape to you, but this work took me years.

You don't have to be into it, but I thought you might at least care why it matters to me.

choices.choiceText: I'm sorry. I was being cynical to sound cool. Please show me the work.
Because watching people obsess over dust motes is amusing to me.
Whatever. Go play with your microphones.

nodes.partnerMessage:
My graduate advisor. He took a bunch of my recordings from an old salt mine project, put his name first, and said the weird readings were just seismic activity.

He got tenure. I lost most of my funding and ended up having to leave the program.

choices.choiceText: That's sickening, Evelyn. Academia can be ruthlessly predatory.
Did you ever try to confront the board with your original timestamps?
Maybe his seismic micro-fracture explanation was actually scientifically sound?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah. That's what it felt like. It taught me to keep the raw stuff private and verify everything twice before I let anyone near it.

I don't want another five years of work turning into somebody else's footnote.

choices.choiceText: You don't have to defend your findings from me. Show me what you salvaged.
I want to help you prove him wrong once and for all.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I tried. I brought in the original reels, timestamps, everything. The dean basically told me I was overreacting and should let it go.

That was the day I decided I was done trusting institutions to protect my work.

choices.choiceText: Being labeled 'hysterical' when you're armed with facts is infuriating.
Let's leave those cowards behind. Show me the observatory data.

nodes.partnerMessage:
...Right. I shouldn't have said anything personal.

I've heard versions of that argument for years, and I guess I was hoping I wouldn't have to hear it from you too.

choices.choiceText: Wait, Evelyn! I didn't mean it like that, I was playing devil's advocate!
If you can't handle objective questioning, your science is weak.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I know what you meant. Just be careful with that one. It's easy to turn 'I'm questioning the idea' into 'I'm questioning you.'

Anyway. Look at this waterfall chart and tell me what you think.

choices.choiceText: Show me the chart. I'll give it an honest, unbiased look.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Thank you. Seriously. I spent years having to prove I wasn't being emotional before anyone would even look at the evidence.

Let's get back to the observatory reel.

choices.choiceText: Lead the way, Evelyn.

nodes.partnerMessage:
That's what I'm trying to do. Not with a dramatic story, either. I want enough clean evidence that nobody can hand-wave it away.

Here's the part I keep coming back to:

choices.choiceText: Unlock the visual feed.

nodes.partnerMessage:
3:14 is when the background noise in that valley is at its lowest. The freight line stops, the radio noise drops, and there isn't much wind.

So I picked that window because it gave me the cleanest recording I could get.

choices.choiceText: The dead hour. When all artificial interference dies out.
And that's when the 18 Hz anomaly emerged?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Pretty much. Everything gets so quiet that little changes stand out.

Honestly, I like being awake then. It's probably the only time my brain stops trying to do ten things at once.

choices.choiceText: Do you spend every night awake during the dead hour?
Show me what the earth was humming that night.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Most nights, yeah. My sleep schedule got wrecked in college and never fully recovered. By 2:30, my apartment is usually dead quiet.

It's kind of nice having someone to talk to during that part of the night, though. I don't usually have that.

choices.choiceText: I'll keep your space capsule company whenever you're drifting.
Sleep deprivation ruins cognitive acuity, Evelyn. You need rest.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Careful. I could get used to that.

I don't let many people into my late-night routine, and now I'm already wondering what it would be like to hear from you at 3 AM tomorrow.

choices.choiceText: Expect them. I'm not going anywhere. Now show me the file.
Let's verify that steady frequency over voice call right now.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I know. You're not wrong.

I just have forty reels waiting on me and some of them really are getting worse with time. It's hard to tell myself to sleep when I know something might be lost while I do.

choices.choiceText: Preserving history is noble, but not at the expense of your health.
Show me the file before you pass out from exhaustion.

nodes.partnerMessage:
...That actually means a lot. Most people ask about the work first and me somewhere after that.

I'm not very good at stopping, but hearing you say that makes me want to try.

choices.choiceText: I care about Evelyn, not just the findings. Show me the spectrogram.

nodes.partnerMessage:
You actually know what that is? Okay, now I'm impressed.

Yes, that's basically the idea. You gently heat the tape so the binder behaves long enough to get a clean transfer. It's one of those things that sounds completely ridiculous until you've ruined a reel without doing it.

choices.choiceText: I care about the craft. Show me what that baked reel revealed.
I care about the girl running the dehydrator even more.
What tape stock was it? Vintage Scotch 206 or old Ampex?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Ampex 456, from 1978. One of the batches that's famous for being a nightmare with the binder.

I was basically holding my breath every time it passed the head. One bad pass and the oxide can start coming off.

choices.choiceText: Restoring that takes surgical nerve. You're brilliant, Evelyn.
Did you manage to transfer it to 24-bit 96kHz before it degraded?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Surgical nerve and way too much black tea. My hands were shaking until the transfer actually finished.

But it worked. At least most of it survived. Let me show you what I got:

choices.choiceText: Unveil it.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I went even cleaner than that. 32-bit float at 192 kHz straight into the converter.

The copy is clean and I kept the original untouched. Here's the visual proof:

choices.choiceText: Show me.

nodes.partnerMessage:
You're really different from the people I used to work with. My old thesis partner used to joke that my field recordings were 'acoustic pareidolia,' then took our grant and moved on.

I haven't let anyone sit beside me while I edit in years.

choices.choiceText: He was blind to what you were building. You're not alone in this room anymore.
Did that betrayal make you put deadbolts on everything?
Well, pareidolia IS a scientific fact in 90% of audio clips.

nodes.partnerMessage: Okay, look at the center of the waterfall, between 03:14:20 and 03:14:45. That's the part I couldn't explain away:

choices.choiceText: Wait... those frequency peaks repeat in an 8-bit binary pattern. How is that possible?
Could be resonant wind flutter cutting through the telescope slit.
Looks like an ordinary compression artifact from exporting to MP3.
What kind of microphone did you use to catch sub-20 Hz frequencies?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Custom pressure transducers with an infrasonic capsule. Regular studio mics fall off pretty hard below 20 Hz, so I needed something built for that range.

This setup can pick up movement down to about 0.5 Hz.

choices.choiceText: Potted in silicone oil to eliminate thermal wind drift... that's genius.
And what did that transducer pick up on the center channel?

nodes.partnerMessage:
You actually know why I did that. That's... weirdly nice.

I spend a lot of time building little things like this alone in my apartment, so having someone understand what went into it feels better than it probably should.

choices.choiceText: I'd rather talk sensor damping with you than party anywhere else.

nodes.partnerMessage:
You noticed the comb filtering. Okay, that's actually really good.

The pattern doesn't behave like a simple background noise source. Something is creating that cancellation pattern, and I still don't have a satisfying answer for it.

choices.choiceText: Or by something trying to push human speech through structural stone.
Let me hear the decoded WAV file over voice call. Let's listen together.
Or someone had a ventilation fan running on a faulty belt.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I checked that first. The transformer serving that ridge was disconnected years before the recording, and there isn't another power line close enough to explain it.

So yeah, I had to cross the easy explanation off the list.

choices.choiceText: That eliminates the power grid. What about a pirate radio transmitter?
I stand corrected. You really did do your homework.
Still could be illegal copper salvage crews running a generator.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Come on. I get that Audacity can make weird things look convincing, but I work from the raw files and keep hashes on them specifically so I can rule out that kind of thing.

That one felt a little dismissive.

choices.choiceText: Evelyn, wait! I was testing your defensive protocols! Don't shut down!
If you get this defensive over software, you know your data is shaky.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Okay. Apology accepted.

I'm used to people making jokes about the work before they actually look at it. So I get defensive faster than I should.

Here. Let's look at the waterfall together.

choices.choiceText: Show me what you've found. I'm completely tuned in.

nodes.partnerMessage: Yeah, no. I'm not doing this with you. Vault access revoked.

Read just now.

Evelyn has muted notifications for this session.

choices.choiceText: Evelyn? You there?
Look, I crossed the line. I'm sorry.
Fine, stay mad in your dusty room.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Read 12m ago.

[Typing...]

Evelyn has gone offline.
User disconnected. Evelyn has permanently revoked your encryption key and blocked your device ID.

...I don't like feeling stupid for caring about something.

If you want to stay here, just treat the work like it matters to me. That's all I'm asking.

choices.choiceText: I do respect it. Show me the spectrogram.

nodes.partnerMessage:
You barely know me yet. You know the girl who gets tape residue on her sleeves and forgets where she left her coffee.

But... I like that you want to know the person, not just the project.

choices.choiceText: That's exactly who I want to know. The girl behind the data.

nodes.partnerMessage:
That hit me harder than I expected.

Some nights it's just me, four monitors, and a bunch of old recordings. I actually do wonder sometimes whether I'm preserving history or just giving myself another reason not to be alone.

choices.choiceText: You're not archiving isolation. You're building a lighthouse. Call me.
Take off the headphones, Evelyn. You don't have to carry the silence alone tonight.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Pretty much. I started keeping everything offline, locked the studio down, and stopped sending unfinished work to journals.

It made me feel safer, but I know it also made it harder to let anyone in.

choices.choiceText: Holding on that tightly must make your hands cramp up.
That sounds exhausting. Do you ever feel like you built your own prison?

nodes.partnerMessage:
It absolutely is. That's why I'm careful with EVP recordings. If you expect to hear a voice, your brain will happily give you one.

I only keep the clips that still seem interesting when the listeners don't know what they're supposed to hear.

choices.choiceText: Double-blind testing... you really are a scientist first.
Let me be your fourth independent listener. Put me on voice call.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Wait—you saw that too?

Look at the peaks. They fall into groups that line up with ASCII, and the word I get is 'STILL.' Same word showed up in another recording from a completely different site.

That's the part I can't stop thinking about.

choices.choiceText: 'Still waiting'... the frequency is an echo looping across fifty years.
Call my phone right now. I need to hear that raw WAV track through my headphones.
Could it be a calibration beacon left behind by telecom engineers?

nodes.partnerMessage:
I thought that too at first. I checked the air movement inside the dome and it was basically dead that night.

The weird part is that the 18 Hz signal still jumped way above the room noise.

choices.choiceText: Then we are officially out of conventional explanations.
What do you think is on the other side of that 18 Hz modulation?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Not MP3. I keep the originals as high-resolution broadcast WAVs.

Sorry. I know that sounded snippy. I just spent way too long making sure the files weren't getting mangled by the format itself.

choices.choiceText: My mistake, Evelyn. I was looking on my phone screen. Tell me more.
Audio file snobs are the most exhausting people alive.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah. That's honestly what it sounded like to me too—something trying to make a voice without having the right shape to make one.

I know how strange that sounds. I'm just relieved you didn't laugh at me for saying it.

choices.choiceText: I'm right here with you, Evelyn. Take my hand across this screen. Call me.
Let me hear that pulse over voice comms. Ring me.

nodes.partnerMessage:
That would give me a pretty different frequency profile. I actually checked the nearby HVAC equipment. Nothing lined up.

You're making me defend this thing harder than I expected, though. 😭

choices.choiceText: You tore my theory to pieces. I respect the acoustic physics.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I looked at that too. A normal radio transmitter doesn't really explain a signal sitting down at 18 Hz, especially not in the way this one shows up.

Still, I'm not ruling out every human source yet. That's kind of the point of the investigation.

choices.choiceText: Propagates through bone... that's why the hair stands up on your neck.
Have you ever felt that nausea yourself on site?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Thanks. That's exactly what I want from people who look at this stuff. Question it. Make me check it again.

I don't want a ghost story just because it's more interesting. I want the explanation that survives.

choices.choiceText: I'll always keep you grounded. Call me and let's run the next file.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I ruled that out too. I checked the ridge with a drone before I went in, and there wasn't any sign of a generator or recent activity.

Could someone have hidden something? Sure. I just didn't find evidence of it.

choices.choiceText: A drone survey before hiking in? You're a full-blown intelligence operative.

nodes.partnerMessage:
...Okay. I'll let that one go.

Just keep the volume sensible when you listen to the tape. It's old enough that I don't want to risk blasting it through damaged headphones for no reason.

choices.choiceText: Headphones are leveled. Connect the voice line.

nodes.partnerMessage:
You really don't know me yet. You know the researcher with chalk on her sleeves, bad sleep habits, and coffee everywhere.

But... maybe that's a start.

choices.choiceText: That's exactly who I want to know. The girl behind the data.

nodes.partnerMessage:
You're making it really hard for me to hide behind the nerdy stuff.

I was going to keep this whole thing professional, and now I'm imagining us sitting on my studio floor eating takeout while the reels run in the background.

Also... I haven't cooked for anyone in a long time.

choices.choiceText: Then let me cook for you. While you bake your tapes, I'll make warm pasta.
Let's start with a voice call first. Hear my voice before you let me in.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I found the original deed from 1912. The observatory used to belong to a private astronomer, Dr. Silas Vance.

He spent years listening to radio noise from Jupiter, which was way ahead of what most people around him were doing. In his last journal entry, he wrote that the mountain was 'singing in a key below my ears.'

choices.choiceText: Singing in a key below his ears... the 18 Hz carrier wave.
What happened to Dr. Vance after that entry?

nodes.partnerMessage:
He died two days later at his desk with his headphones on. The local paper called it heart failure and left it at that.

What got me interested was finding one of his old crystal detectors in the county historical society. I couldn't believe they still had it.

choices.choiceText: You tracked down his actual detector?! Evelyn, that's forensic gold.
Did you hook it up to modern preamps to see if it still resonates?

nodes.partnerMessage:
I know. Finding it was ridiculous luck.

I hooked it up to an oscilloscope and got a pattern that looked surprisingly similar to the one from the mountain recording. That's when this stopped feeling like a collection of unrelated weird things.

choices.choiceText: A Lissajous figure... a geometric fingerprint preserved across ninety years.
Show me the trace. Call me so we can look at it live.

nodes.partnerMessage:
First thing I did. I put it in a shielded setup because I didn't want a cell tower or some random nearby signal messing with the test.

And somehow I still got a tiny signal from it with nothing connected to power.

choices.choiceText: That defies basic electromagnetic conservation of energy unless it's scavenging RF.

nodes.partnerMessage:
That's my current theory. Some kind of environmental or geological source could be feeding a tiny amount of energy into the system.

I'm still testing it, though. I don't want to call it solved just because one explanation sounds cool.

choices.choiceText: You are a genuine scientific visionary, Evelyn.

nodes.partnerMessage:
...That's not a word I hear very often. Usually it's obsessive, difficult, or just 'too much.'

I don't know. Hearing it from you makes me want to keep going.

choices.choiceText: Then let me call you tonight so you can hear me say it out loud.

nodes.partnerMessage:
It looked almost too clean. Just this repeating loop, over and over.

It made me think about how much of the past disappears just because nobody bothered to keep the recording, the notes, or the person's voice. I guess that's part of why I care so much about this stuff.

choices.choiceText: You didn't forget them. And I won't forget you, Evelyn. Let's get on voice call.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Okay. Headphones are off.

...Wow. It's actually quieter than I thought. I can hear the rain, the hard drive fan, and nothing else.

This is nice. Weirdly nice. It feels different knowing someone is actually on the other side of the screen.

choices.choiceText: Keep them off for the night, Evelyn. Let me be your quiet peace. Call me.
I'm right here. Let's connect over voice so you don't feel alone.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah. Sometimes I look at all the locks and cameras and realize I've basically built a place where nobody can hurt my work... but nobody gets close either.

I don't always know which part scares me more.

choices.choiceText: Let me unlock the door from the outside, Evelyn. Step into the light with me.
You don't have to risk getting hurt with me. Call me and let me prove it.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Exactly. Otherwise you're just finding what you already wanted to find.

I need evidence that still looks interesting when someone tries really hard to disprove it. That's the part I care about most.

choices.choiceText: I'll be your scientific collaborator. Let's inspect the files on voice.

nodes.partnerMessage:
That's what makes it so unsettling. Same signal, different place, decades apart.

Maybe it's coincidence. Maybe it's something physical we haven't figured out. But I can't pretend I don't find the pattern fascinating.

choices.choiceText: We heard it, Evelyn. Let's listen to the full reel together over voice comms.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I considered that. The timing and modulation don't really match the systems I'm familiar with, though.

Still, that's a fair question. I'd rather test another theory than dismiss it because I don't like it.

choices.choiceText: Fair enough. Your knowledge of radio regulations is terrifyingly complete.

nodes.partnerMessage:
This is where I get uncomfortable. Once I've ruled out the obvious stuff, I'm left with something I can't explain yet.

And honestly, that's more interesting to me than pretending I already know the answer.

choices.choiceText: Something that didn't have lungs... give me your voice line. Let's listen.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Sometimes I wonder if we're looking at a kind of recording process we don't understand yet. Not a ghost exactly. More like a place somehow holding onto what happened there.

I know that sounds out there. I'm still trying to figure out how much of it I actually believe.

choices.choiceText: Stone Tape Theory, elevated by modern acoustic physics. Beautiful.
If the mountain records memories, what is it recording between us tonight?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Alright. Reset. I know I get too hung up on the technical details when I care about something.

The thing I'm looking at is the pattern in the center of the waterfall. See the little groups of peaks?

choices.choiceText: I see the 18 Hz binary modulation. It spells out 'STILL'.

nodes.partnerMessage:
That feeling is real, at least in the sense that your body can react to very low frequencies before you're consciously aware of them.

It's one reason people sometimes say they 'felt' something was wrong before they could explain why.

choices.choiceText: My body definitely knows you're special, Evelyn. Ring my line.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Once, in an old boiler tunnel. I got dizzy, my vision started going gray, and the recorder showed a big infrasonic spike around 19 Hz.

I had to get back outside on my hands and knees. I was alone, and that part still bothers me more than the weird reading does.

choices.choiceText: You crawled in the dark alone?! Promise me you will never go into a tunnel without me.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Okay, that title is definitely going to my head.

I just like knowing what I'm walking into before I enter somewhere sketchy. My friends call it overkill. I call it not getting stuck underground at 2 AM.

choices.choiceText: Then let's form an operational unit. Hit my voice call button.

nodes.partnerMessage:
That sounds... really nice. Pasta, rain outside, reels running in the background.

I can't remember the last time this room felt like somewhere you could actually relax in.

choices.choiceText: I'm going to take care of you, Evelyn. Call me tonight so we can plan it.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah. That's what gets me. He heard something nobody around him could make sense of, and then he was gone two days later.

I don't know what happened to him, but I keep thinking about that last note every time I hear the same frequency now.

choices.choiceText: And you're the one finishing his symphony. Let me listen with you.

nodes.partnerMessage:
...Okay. I'm trying.

I think I've been waiting for someone to ask me to open the door without also asking me to stop being who I am.

Call me. I want to hear your voice before I get nervous and change my mind.

choices.choiceText: Calling you right now, Evelyn. Pick up.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Okay. Deal. No more tunnels alone.

I'll take the telemetry, you handle the flashlight. And... it actually feels good knowing somebody would care whether I made it back out.

choices.choiceText: Always by your side. Now ring my line, partner.

nodes.partnerMessage:
You know about it? Okay, you officially have my attention.

I don't agree with every version of the theory, but I think the idea is interesting enough to test instead of just laugh at. That's basically how I approach all of this.

choices.choiceText: Then let's co-author the future together. Hit the call button.

nodes.partnerMessage:
...That's a dangerous question.

Probably this conversation. Me sitting here smiling at my screen like an idiot instead of looking at the monitor.

Maybe that's what the mountain would keep if it could actually record us.

choices.choiceText: Let the universe shrink. As long as you and I are in it. Call me.

nodes.partnerMessage:
...They do. My hands get stiff after long nights of splicing tape, and I've been staring at waveforms for way too many hours lately.

Sometimes I think I just want someone to tell me I can stop for the night and not feel guilty about it.

choices.choiceText: It's okay to sleep, Evelyn. I've got the watch tonight. Call me.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Okay, voice is ready.

Hit the call button before I overthink this.

choices.choiceText: Initiating secure audio link...

nodes.partnerMessage: Okay, I see it ringing. Pick up, {PlayerName}.

Did the call drop?

I'm still here. Try again when you're ready.

choices.choiceText: Carrier dropped for a second! Calling you right back!
Got goosebumps from the static tone, but I'm dialed in now.

nodes.partnerMessage:
This is nice. Sitting here with the rain outside, your car warm, and Vance's ledger safe with me... I don't feel like I need to keep checking over my shoulder for once.

I spent a long time keeping everyone out. Somehow you got me to open the door anyway. Take us home, {PlayerName}.
